tools.description: Return artifact metadata and content_base64 bytes for a sha256 the caller workspace can access. A missing access ref is NotFound. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_artifact

tools.description: What the thread's current review was handed, recorded when it went to review: the thread version, the result's content hash and the linked artifacts' hashes, with the evidence root over them. Each item carries an attestation tier judged at the hand-off: verified (a land-gate pass the close gate accepts), attached (linked by a member who never worked the thread) or self_reported (a worker's own result or link). self_reported_only is true when every item is self-reported. Null before any review. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_review_packet

tools.description: Read a thread's review standing: required_count, approvals (distinct qualifying), and approvals_met. This is the approval side of the close-gate; a refutes edge is checked separately when closing.
tools.name: get_review_status

tools.description: Pack thread messages, edits, references, FSM history, and the workspace glossary for agent prompts. Edits are lean by default (id/editor/timestamp only); pass include_edits=true for full before/after bodies. The glossary (canonical term definitions) is included by default when non-empty; pass include_glossary=false to drop it. Pass as_of=<event_id> to replay the thread as it stood at that event-log id (deterministic over the immutable log; audit / re-ask from before a tangent). Pass token_budget=<n> to cap the message page by estimated tokens: the opening message and the recent tail are kept, the middle is folded into an auditable elision marker in fixed blocks. The result is two text parts: the stable prefix (workspace boot, brief, messages) and the volatile tail (state, lease, cursors, prefix sha256). Those strings are the bytes REST returns with split=true.

as_of.description: Event-log id: reconstruct the thread as it stood at that point (as-of replay). Omit for the live pack.

delta.description: Return a delta instead of the whole pack. The first content part is always the delta head (delta, prefix_unchanged, prefix_sha256, prefix_bytes), never empty; the second is the volatile tail. When since_prefix_sha matches the current prefix, the head has prefix_unchanged true and no messages or prefix. With message_cursor, the head adds the messages after that cursor when appending them rebuilds the prefix; otherwise it carries the replacement prefix.

include_accepted_decisions.description: Attach in-channel accepted/closed decisions (token-lean teasers) so a fresh claimer sees what the channel already decided. Waiter envelopes appear only when status is reviewed; result_kind is a namespaced string (e.g. example.review.result/1), not a closed enum. Withheld on DM channels. Set false for the leanest pack.

include_edits.description: Include full body_before/body_after on each edit (heavy); default returns edit metadata only.

include_glossary.description: Include the workspace glossary (grounding); omitted when empty. Set false for a token-tight pack.

include_parent_grounding.description: For a child thread, attach parent grounding (the parent's opening ask + latest decision) so a fresh claimer knows why the thread exists. Absent for root threads / cross-channel / DM parents. Set false for the leanest pack.

max_bytes.description: Cap the canonical pack by bytes. Elision grows by fixed message blocks until the pack fits or only the opener and newest message remain.

message_cursor.description: Page messages after this id. With delta, it is also the delta cursor.

since_prefix_sha.description: Hex sha256 of a prefix the caller already holds. Requests a delta on its own.

token_budget.description: Cap the message page by estimated tokens (chars/4): keep the opening message and the recent tail, fold the middle into an auditable 'elision' marker. Omit to cap by rows only.

tools.name: get_thread_context

tools.description: Read a task's structured result, or null if none has been produced yet.
tools.name: get_thread_result

tools.description: The waiting-on-you inbox, everything needing a member's attention: their assigned non-terminal threads, the reviews requested from them (review_request: a thread in review naming them as a reviewer, without their approval yet), the reviews that name no reviewer and fall to them (unassigned_review: a thread in review with no named reviewer that they own, or that nobody owns when they are a workspace admin), the workspace's pending approval gates, and their unread mentions. Oldest-waiting first, each aged against sla_secs (default 86400 = 24h) with an overdue flag. One member's queue, not @everyone. For mentions alone, with a read-cursor you advance with mark_inbox_read, use get_inbox.
tools.name: get_waiting_inbox

tools.description: List the messages in a thread, oldest first, excluding withdrawn (tombstoned) ones. Each message has id, author_id, body, metadata, content, posted_at, edited_at and origin. It returns the first limit messages with no cursor, so a long thread's later messages are not reachable here; use get_thread_context for a prompt-ready pack with message cursors and a token budget, or search_messages to find messages by text. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return, counted from the oldest. Defaults to 100; values outside 1 to 500 are clamped into that range.

thread_id.description: UUID of the thread whose messages to list.

tools.name: list_messages

tools.description: List each reviewer's current decision on a thread, ordered by creation time. A row has reviewer_id, decision (approve or request_changes), note, the delegate actor_id if one submitted it, evidence_root, head_sha and dismissed_at, which is set on an approval that a later change request invalidated. Re-submitting replaces a reviewer's row, so earlier verdicts are in list_review_history; whether the requirement is met is in get_review_status. Submit with submit_review. Requires workspace:read and read access to the thread's channel.

thread_id.description: UUID of the thread whose review decisions to list.

tools.name: list_reviews

tools.description: The artifacts linked to the thread as evidence, in the order they were linked, each with who linked it. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: list_thread_artifacts

tools.description: Post a message to a thread as the authenticated member and return the stored message (id, thread_id, author_id, body, metadata, content, posted_at). Send body for plain text or content for typed blocks; when body is empty it is derived from the blocks, and sending neither is refused. A closed thread still takes messages, while a deleted or archived thread refuses them. The post appends a MessagePosted event, records each @handle mention and publishes a mention event for it, and runs the registered slash command when the body begins with /name (see register_slash_command). For a DM conversation id use post_dm_message. Requires message:post.

body.description: Plain-text message text, which is what search indexes. Omit it or send an empty string when you pass content. At least one of body or content is required.

content.description: Typed content blocks in order. Each block has a type: text {text}, code {code, language}, tool_use {id, name, input}, tool_result {tool_use_id, content, is_error}, or resource_link {uri, mime_type, title}. When body is empty, body is built from the blocks; tool_use blocks add no text.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON object stored with the message and returned with it, for example {"artifacts": ["<sha256>"]} to name artifacts the message refers to. Defaults to an empty object.

thread_id.description: UUID of the thread to post in. You must be able to read it; a thread in a private channel or DM you are not part of is refused.

tools.name: post_message

tools.description: Submit a review decision as the caller (G5): approve or request_changes. The reviewer is you; an owner/assignee may submit but it will not count toward the requirement (separation of duties). request_changes on an in_review thread, from its owner or a reviewer whose approval would count, sends it back to open for rework: it is claimable again, earlier approvals are dismissed, and your note appears in its context as change_requests. request_changes needs a note saying what to change; approve may carry one. approve also needs evidence_root, the root from get_review_packet of what you were shown: it is refused when the thread was handed over again or changed since, and only an approval bound to the latest packet counts toward the close. Every verdict appends a review_submitted event (the note stays in the review history), and a request_changes notifies the thread's last worker. Re-submitting changes your decision. Requires thread:transition.

evidence_root.description: the evidence_root from get_review_packet you are deciding on, required on approve

head_sha.description: optional full commit SHA of the change head you reviewed; refused as a conflict when the change has moved since

note.description: what to change, required on request_changes; optional on approve

tools.name: submit_review

tools.description: Advance a thread's FSM state (start_review, close, or archive). The MCP twin of REST POST /threads/:id. Separation of duties, the required-reviewers close-gate, and unresolved refutes all apply identically — there is no MCP bypass. On a thread with a review requirement, start_review is refused until a result is posted (set_thread_result). Returns the updated thread.

action.description: start_review (open to in_review), close (in_review to closed) or archive (closed to archived). To send work back, use submit_review with request_changes

tools.name: transition_thread

tools.description: Block until the member has an unread notification of any kind (a mention, or an event routed to them as owner or follower), or the timeout lapses. Reads the notification ledger, so it also returns a row written while you were not waiting: pass since_log_id (the highest source_log_id you have seen) and it returns the oldest unread notification after it; omit it to wait for one newer than this call. Returns that notification with the thread's title and a short reason, or null on timeout. Never marks it read.

since_log_id.description: return the oldest unread notification whose source_log_id is greater than this, including one written before the call; omitted, only notifications for events after the call

tools.name: wait_for_notification

tools.description: Return the authentication-bound identity: actor_id, member_id, optional delegation_grant_id, workspace_id, capabilities, capability_sets the caller fully holds, and whether the credential is a bearer. Call this first — writes are attributed to member_id.
tools.name: whoami
